newsitem.title: USA: Taiwan may import veg/soyoil instead beans - attache.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may import veg/soyoil instead beans - attache.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache said Taiwan may import crude soybean oil or other vegetable oils instead of importing soybeans to meet domestic cooking oil demand in the near future.

"It is hard to predict when it will happen, but the trade estimates that importing soybean oil in bulk is profitable when domestic soybean oil price is 10-20 percent higher than the world soybean oil level, the attache wrote in a report dated April 16.

The attache said due to the current high soybean world price level and declining domestic demand of soybean meal caused by the foot-and-mouth epidemic among hogs, Taiwan crushers were planning to raise their prices 20 percent ex-factory, which may stimulate further price increases.
Taiwan MY97/98 soybean oil imports are estimated at 40,000 tonnes, the attache said.

The attache said based on soybean oil's characteristics and its price competitiveness, it was unlikely that palm oil and other types of vegetable oil could replace it in its biggest market, sales to restaurants, hospitals and institutions.
